newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebels take key Zaire bridge, reports say.
newsitem.headline: Rebels take key Zaire bridge, reports say.

text.p: Laurent Kabila's rebels have taken a key bridge on the road to Zaire's capital Kinshasa, reports reaching the city said on Tuesday.
Zaireans from the region, in contact with residents there by radio, said government forces pulled back from the Kwango River Bridge about 180 km (110 miles) by road from the capital on Monday.

Information Minister Kin-Kiey Mulumba told Reuters he could make no immediate comment on the reports. On Monday, he told reporters there was fierce fighting in the region of Kenge, 60 km (40 miles) to the east.

"The FAZ (Armed Forces of Zaire) abandoned the Kwango Bridge. We heard about it yesterday," one Zairian dignitary from the region told Reuters. "The army fell back to Mbankana, about 150 km (100 miles) from Kinshasa."
The source said the rebels were not sticking to the main road. "Kabila's men are infiltrating the region. They are not using the paved road."

Kin-Kiey Mulumba said on Monday after a special cabinet meeting that there had been violent fighting in the region of Kenge, which is 200 km (125 miles) from Kinshasa as the crow flies and longer by road.
"The fighting is very violent," he told state radio. "The FAZ are busy maintaining the front line and pushing it back."

The rebels, who admit facing stiff resistance, have been talking tough ahead of Wednesday talks between President Mobutu Sese Seko and Kabila. Kabila says Mobutu must hand over power if he wants to avoid a battle for the capital.
